description: Findings judged real but not fixed by the task that found them. Read by the lead at each post-task review, and promoted into tasks/prd.json when worth doing. Not part of any task's brief: no role file or doc points subagents here.

conventions.status: open | check (may already be fixed) | promoted (to the prd task named in notes) | wontfix (reason in notes)
conventions.source: the task whose review found it, or the review that did

items.title: helper slot protection is a count, not a reservation
OutputVersion bump invalidates every stored segment
GET /Sessions shows a helper's worker and speed as the viewer's
helpers spawn helpers
no reason shown to operators when a burnt-image job gets no helpers
helper placement counts slots, not CPU
helper jobs indistinguishable from seeks and failovers for operators
paused helpers keep their slots; a second new viewer can queue
No check covers the PlaybackInfo admission path (Jobs.Unavailable)
transcodeHelpers reaching Worker.NoHelpers has no executable check
transcodeHelpers is per worker, so mixed settings leave helpers running
A helper preempted mid-chunk leaves a gap the asking job never fills
Every ensure takes one cluster-wide advisory lock
Preempting a helper when it cannot free a slot for the viewer
Every running helper beats on any preempt hint
No check drives the transcodeHelpers config key to the worker
A helper preempted during pre-ffmpeg setup sees the cancel only after ffmpeg starts
The e2e HDR10 copy scenario never runs in CI (needs E2E_HEVC=1)
DV 7 fixture has no enhancement-layer NALs
Roll-order check pins docs wording, not behaviour
4K HDR TrueHD criterion has no check (lead measured 73x on 4 CPUs)
Capture note cites a TrueHD observation its JSON lacks
AV1 HDR copies have no ffmpeg-path test
Copy of both opens the source twice; one input splices the same (deferred to JS-074)
items.notes: Deferred to JS-074, which is done; confirm whether it was fixed there

items.title: SecondaryAudioNotSupported not named for a track pick
MP3 under Chrome re-encoded where Jellyfin copies (fMP4 only)
Copied audio list taken from the h264 HLS profile for HEVC/AV1 copies
No check pins the re-encoded-audio copy to two inputs
A track ffmpeg hangs on until the time limit leaves the film's good text tracks unstored (documented limit; a fallback would read the picked track alone after a timeout)
The first pick of a track the pass could not extract answers 'its result is missing'
A track the file lacks is logged as 'ffmpeg can't extract it'
Each text track the file lacks costs an ffmpeg start, which on S3 is an open and a header read
docs/subtitles.md gives no number for a proxy's read timeout during a subtitle pass (up to twice SubtitleTimeout)
One slot pool counts a near-free copy the same as a multi-core re-encode (internal/transcode/worker.go slots); fold into JS-054's design and before JS-057's scaling signal
The scan decides what to re-probe from stored JSON with a special case per feature (internal/library/scan.go); a probe_version would replace the shims, before JS-045
The 1600-stream control-plane ceiling was measured on empty tables; ended-job lookups and the sweep's delete by created_at are unindexed (amend JS-030)
No way to ask for a scan, a re-probe or an asset rebuild, which a restore needs (amend JS-059)
The Store interface has no Stat (callers open to check existence), and S3 has one credential pair for every store (JS-055, JS-056)
Worker.encode is a 400-line function whose loop interleaves six concerns; split before JS-029 next changes it
JS-054 is too large for one build: slice detection and one family (Intel QSV/VAAPI on the dogfood) from placement and failover
JS-021 is too large and blocks JS-057; JS-062's gate is undefined for a 4-CPU homelab
Start and seek times have no stated target and no recorded trend (first-frame times are logged in test/e2e/transcode.mjs, not recorded)
Nothing plans for the next Jellyfin release: jellyfin/jellyfin:12.4 is pinned in three places with no procedure to move
DOMAINS.md is 117 KB with lines over 14,000 characters; every role reads it
JS-070 derives required fields with a script instead of using the client SDKs as the oracle, and the differential tier masks playlist content
JS-030 is a grab-bag; the one-reaper item is not needed at the target scale (ARCHITECTURE.md rule 6)
A DVB cue that ends by its page time-out, with no clear packet, is treated as showing forever
items.notes: imagecues.go classify ignores page_time_out; a run long after such a cue opens at its start and reads the gap. Reading only.

items.title: A film whose image-track Cues cannot be parsed has them re-read and warned about on every scan
items.notes: No marker for unreadable; image_cues stays NULL and loadSeen selects it again.

items.title: A seek inside a long-showing image cue pays the cue's whole age, uncapped
items.notes: Measured 0.3 MB and 0.04 s per second of age at 640x360; a 4K film costs more and is unmeasured. A cap would drop a cue on screen, so it needs a viewer-visible decision.
